title: text_ledger.py reports wrong line numbers for 737 of 892 card comment units
claim: tools/audit/text_ledger.py:scan_c_like drops one line from its counter each time a JavaScript quote is cut off at a newline, so 737 of the card's 892 D5 units carry a line up to 11 lines away from where the unit sits.
mechanism: In the string branch, an unterminated ' or " (an apostrophe inside a regex literal or a comment-adjacent token) breaks at the newline and sets i = j + 1, consuming the newline without line += 1; the drift accumulates down the file. Unit ids hash the text and are unaffected, but every ledger 'line' column and any harness locating code beside a unit by that line reads the wrong place (this seat's own adjacent-constant check did until it relocated units).

evidence.unit: units whose reported line is not their file line
evidence.contention_note: shared box during the fan-out; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: one-line instrument edit, applied in memory by ledger_lines.py --patched: in scan_c_like's string loop, 'break' -> 'line += 1; break' for an unterminated non-template quote
perturbation.observed_value: misplaced_units 737 -> 1, max_offset 11 -> 1 (the residual 1 is a locator tie)

metric_definition: Card D5 units whose text_ledger line differs from the file line where the unit's first text line is found, searching forward from the previous unit.
phenomenon_property: text_ledger.py's line column is the file line of the unit it names, for every C-like file it scans.

null_control.note: the same locator with the one-line fix; Python units (tokenize) are not affected

proposed_fix_scope: tools/audit/text_ledger.py:scan_c_like count the newline an unterminated quote stops at (and an escaped newline); add a self-test arm with an apostrophe in a regex literal. The file sits in D5-s6's cells; the defect was met measuring D5-s4's card.
